objective: Deep comparative analysis of buyer assistance algorithms in global and local products vs. in-depth audit of Kalam proprietary algorithms
audience: Torob Hackathon Judges, Product Engineers, Algorithm Architects
questions: Q1: How do global leaders (Google Local Inventory, Instacart Aisle Routing, Target In-Store Mode, Amazon Dash Cart/Rufus) solve buyer assistance and physical navigation?
Q2: How do Iranian platforms (Digikala, Snapp/SnappPay, Neshan/Balad, Torob) handle in-person shopping, and where are the structural gaps?
Q3: How do our own 7 Kalam algorithms (IP-CRP, PACO, IMWP, CrediPay, INDP, SVDP, TFRA) function mathematically and architecturally?
Q4: What does the feature-by-feature comparative matrix reveal regarding Kalam competitive moat?
Q5: What are the edge cases, vulnerabilities, and hardening strategies for our own algorithms?
scope: Global retail/ecommerce/mapping products, Iranian tech platforms, and Kalam algorithm specifications
constraints: Contextualized for Tehran urban and commercial realities

acceptance.description: Exhaustive anatomical breakdown of global buyer assistance systems and their routing/inventory mechanisms
acceptance.required_evidence_kind: technical architecture analysis and algorithmic comparisons

acceptance.description: Deep audit of Iranian ecosystem and structural in-person gaps
acceptance.required_evidence_kind: local platform teardown and pain point analysis

acceptance.description: Mathematical and operational deconstruction of Kalam 7 core algorithms
acceptance.required_evidence_kind: formulas, pseudo-code, and dataset integration proofs

acceptance.description: Comprehensive multi-dimensional comparison matrix and defensible competitive moat synthesis
acceptance.required_evidence_kind: matrix tables and strategic differentiation analysis

acceptance.description: Self-critique, algorithmic stress tests, and mitigation architectures
acceptance.required_evidence_kind: failure modes analysis and hardening specifications
